• The duration of labor is variable. In the first stage of labor or stage of dilatation, the cervix of the uterus is dilated and as a rule, the amnion is ruptured, and the amniotic fluid is expelled. During the second stage of labor or stage of descent, the child descends through the vagina and is expelled. The third stage of labor is the placental stage during this the membranes of the fetus are expelled. The sixth stage is of a typical vertex or cephalic (head-first presentation) delivery:
    • Engagement of the fetal head in the transverse position. The baby's head is facing across the pelvis at one or other of the mother's hips.
    • Descent and flexion of the fetal head.
    • Internal rotation. The fetal head rotates 90 degrees to the occipital-anterior position so that the baby's face is toward the mother's rectum.
    • Delivery by extension. The fetal head is bowed, chin on chest, so that the back or crown of its head leads the way through the birth canal, until the back of its neck pressed against the pubic bone and its chin leaves its chest, extending the neck - as if to look up, and the rest of its head passes out of the birth canal.
    • Restitution: The fetal head turns through 45 degrees to restore its normal relationship with the shoulders, which are still at an angle.
    • External rotation: The shoulders repeat the corkscrew movements of the head, which can be seen in the final movements of the fetal head. By this sequence, it can be understood that the last cardinal movement (before expulsion) is external rotation.
    • Mnemonic to remember cardinal moments of labor is (Every Day Fine Infants Enter Eager and Excited).

·         Serum Ferritin is the best test to detect iron deficiency in a client. It measures the amount of ferritin in the serum. The test is done to find out the total iron storage capacity of the body, to diagnose iron deficiency or overload of iron. The ferritin test is ordered when the hemoglobin test and hematocrit indicate that the hemoglobin is less and the RBCs are paler and smaller than usual.

·         Principle: Ferritin is a major iron protein and is the primary form of iron stored in the cells.  A very small amount of ferritin is released and circulate in the body. So, assessing ferritin is an indirect way to measure iron stored in a body. The iron must be absorbed in the body that one takes as a supplement or with foodstuffs. Normally iron incorporated in the body with hemoglobin of RBCs and other is stored as ferritin or as hemosiderin along with other proteins like myoglobin. Ferritin and hemosiderin are present mainly in liver and bone marrow, skeletal muscles, and spleen.

·         Indications: Low level of ferritin-When the level of iron drops in a body, ferritin level drops. The reason for this drop-in level may be because of:

o    When food is deficient in iron

o    The body is not absorbing iron like in celiac disease

o    Or the body has increased demand like in pregnancy, chronic blood loss as in colon cancer, or during childhood.

·         High level of ferritin: There may be an elevated level of ferritin in the body when the iron is in excess like in hereditary hemochromatosis. In such cases, the intestine absorbs iron in a high amount which accumulates in the body. The high iron content gets deposited in joints, heart, liver, and testicles in men. The organs with iron deposit dysfunction. Ferritin levels can increase during inflammation in the body.

·         Advantages:

o    It can be done at any time of the day without any special preparation.

o    The test sample is taken from vein-like any other routine blood test.

o    It is an indirect way to know about the store of iron in the body and is often ordered in routine.

o    Ferrous sulphate is a type of iron that is used to treat iron deficiency and it is also used to test drugs in pharmacology.

o    A serum iron test is done to measure the total iron-binding capacity in the blood.

• The most common occupational hazard that occurs because of working for long hours on the computer is "carpal tunnel syndrome. It is neuropathy that can occur due to excessive movements of hand resulting in pain, paresthesia, numbness of the hand, and weakness of fingers that occurs due to the compression of the median nerve.
  • Cancer is the uncontrolled division of cells that occurs due to the presence of any carcinogenic factors. There is no such factor associated with the use of computers.
  • Lung disease occurs as a result of exposure to allergens or factors affecting the respiratory system through inhalation like dust, fumes, or aerosols. While using computer such allergens are not encountered.
  • A cataract is an eye disorder characterized by opacity or cloudiness of the lens. It can occur because of advanced age, related to myopia, and excessive sunlight exposure but nothing related to the use of computers. Excessive time on the computer can cause dryness of eyes or eye fatigue but not a cataract.

Reference:

  1.  Brunner and Suddarth’s, Textbook of Medical-Surgical Nursing, 10thedition, 2004, pp. 316,552,1761,2052]

choices.title: Surgical scissor
choices.correct_explanation:
• Surgical scissors are sterilized most commonly by autoclave or steam sterilization.
  • Surgical scissors are categorized under critical instrument heading because they penetrate the tissue or contact the bloodstream, which is otherwise sterile.
  • Suction catheter, enema tube, and nasogastric tube come under semi-critical category and can be taken care of by cleaning with soapy water and hydrogen peroxide.

 

Reference:

  1. Ananthanarayan and Paniker’s, Textbook of Microbiology, 2018, 10th edition, pp. 35-7
